classification.difficultyReason: Construct diagrams connecting related-angle cosine identities with unit-circle coordinates and cosine-graph symmetry.

answer.short: Reflection in the $y$-axis reverses the horizontal coordinate, so $\cos(180^{\circ}-\theta)=-\cos\theta$.
answer.worked:
On the unit circle, let $P=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$. Reflecting $P$ in the $y$-axis gives $Q=(-\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$ at angle $180^{\circ}-\theta$. Cosine is the horizontal coordinate, so $\cos(180^{\circ}-\theta)=-\cos\theta$.

The cosine graph shows equal distances from the horizontal axis on opposite sides at $\theta$ and $180^{\circ}-\theta$.

spec.mathematics: The points at theta and 180 degrees minus theta have opposite horizontal coordinates.

spec.description: Cosine curve with opposite signed ordinates at theta and 180 degrees minus theta; matching double ticks indicate equal magnitudes.
spec.mathematics: cos(180 degrees minus theta) equals negative cos(theta).

answer.short: A half-turn about the origin reverses the horizontal coordinate, so $\cos(180^{\circ}+\theta)=-\cos\theta$.
answer.worked:
On the unit circle, let $P=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$. Rotating $P$ through $180^{\circ}$ about the origin gives $Q=(-\cos\theta,-\sin\theta)$ at angle $180^{\circ}+\theta$. Their horizontal coordinates are opposites, so $\cos(180^{\circ}+\theta)=-\cos\theta$.

On the cosine graph, the ordinates at $\theta$ and $180^{\circ}+\theta$ have equal magnitudes and opposite signs.

spec.mathematics: A half-turn negates both coordinates, including cosine.

spec.mathematics: The cosine ordinates separated by 180 degrees are opposites.

answer.short: Reflection in the $x$-axis preserves the horizontal coordinate, so $\cos(360^{\circ}-\theta)=\cos\theta$.
answer.worked:
On the unit circle, let $P=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$. Reflecting $P$ in the $x$-axis gives $Q=(\cos\theta,-\sin\theta)$ at angle $360^{\circ}-\theta$. Their horizontal coordinates are equal, so $\cos(360^{\circ}-\theta)=\cos\theta$.

The cosine graph has equal ordinates at $\theta$ and $360^{\circ}-\theta$, symmetrically placed about $180^{\circ}$.
